race.name: Core4
race.tagline: 120 miles of Iowa gravel, B-roads and singletrack, now a round of The Traka World Series.

climate.description: The 2025 edition started in the high 60s with showers and reached a 114°F heat index with no shade and little wind. Overnight storms that year forced the wet-weather route.
challenges: Storms that turn B-roads to mud

terrain.primary: Eastern Iowa gravel, B-roads and singletrack
terrain.surface: Gravel roads, unmaintained B-roads, singletrack and pavement, with urban bike paths on the way back to Iowa City. Rolling 5-7% grades leave few flat miles. The wet-weather route trims singletrack and swaps in grassy B-road alternates.
features: Solo or team-of-three entry on the long routes

gravel_god_rating.score_note: CORE4 lands in Tier 2 on 120 miles, about 6,000 feet, real B-road and singletrack variety, late-August heat and a pro race that now carries Traka World Series points. It stays below Tier 1 because it is a five-edition regional event whose routes and aid details arrive only weeks before the start.

biased_opinion.summary: CORE4 is 120 miles and about 6,000 feet of Iowa gravel, B-roads, singletrack and pavement, and in 2027 it is a round of The Traka World Series. The racing is real: the 2026 edition paid a $15,000 Pro/Elite purse. The catch is timing. Routes and aid locations go public in early August, and late-August heat can turn the day into a hydration test.
strengths: Round 5 of The Traka World Series in 2027
B-roads, singletrack, pavement and a CX-style finish in one route
Team-of-three category on the long routes
weaknesses: Wet B-roads turn to sticky mud
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Race it for the pro field and the B-roads, and arrive heat-adapted.

final_verdict.one_liner: 120 miles of Iowa gravel and B-roads with a Traka World Series pro race up front.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a late-summer US race with a real pro field and mixed terrain. Skip it if you need the GPX months out; routes publish in early August.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a longer late-summer Midwest race, compare Gravel Worlds. For the Traka format at full size, The Traka in Girona.

logistics.airport: The Eastern Iowa Airport (CID) in Cedar Rapids is the closest commercial airport.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Book Iowa City early; the 2026 edition had camping near the Wilson's Orchard venue.
logistics.food: Iowa City has full dining and grocery options.

history.origin_story: CORE4 debuted in 2022 as a sister event to Bentonville's Rule of Three, borrowing its multi-distance, team-of-three format and building a course from singletrack, pavement, Iowa B-roads and a cyclocross-style finish.
notable_moments: 2025: overnight storms forced the wet-weather route, and B-road mud split the fields
2026: Gravel Earth Series stop with a $15,000 Pro/Elite purse; Geerike Schreurs won solo and Tobias Kongstad won the sprint
2027: round 5 of The Traka World Series
history.reputation: Iowa's B-road race, now with a European pro series attached.

course_description.character: The 2027 routes are not public yet. The 2026 course started on Main Street in Solon, north of Iowa City, and mixed gravel, B-roads, singletrack and pavement past river crossings, prairie savannah and an urban section. The organizer lists about 6,000 feet for the 120-mile route.
course_description.signature_challenge: Racing the B-roads in whatever state the weather left them: dust when dry, sticky mud after storms.
course_description.edition_note: Distances and approximate climbing are confirmed for 2027. The organizer publishes routes and aid locations in early August, so 2026 and 2025 course details describe character, not the 2027 line.

migration_notes: 2026-11-05: Added as a new profile after The Traka World Series named CORE4 round 5 for 2027. Organizer confirms August 20-21, 2027 and the 120-mile flagship at about 6,000 feet; routes and prices are not yet published.

logistics.explanation: Easy by US standards. Iowa City is a drive-in college town, and the 2026 edition finished at Wilson's Orchard with camping near the venue [5].

length.explanation: A full day. The flagship is 120 miles, with 70-, 40- and 20-mile options below it [2].

technicality.explanation: Mixed terrain with teeth. The course combines gravel, B-roads, singletrack and pavement [3], and in 2025 wet B-roads packed tires with mud and split the field [7].

elevation.explanation: Iowa is not flat here. The organizer lists about 6,000 feet for the 120-mile route [2], and rolling 5-7% grades leave almost nowhere to recover [7].

climate.explanation: Late August in Iowa is a heat test. The 2025 edition hit a 114°F heat index with no shade [7], and the race runs rain or shine with a wet-weather route on standby [2].

altitude.explanation: Irrelevant. This is eastern Iowa river country around Iowa City [1].

adventure.explanation: Good regional character, not a pilgrimage. River crossings, prairie savannah, an urban section and an orchard finish give the day variety [3], but the scenery alone won't justify a flight.

prestige.explanation: A regional race with a fast-rising profile. It started in 2022 [6], was a Gravel Earth Series stop in 2026 [5], and is round 5 of The Traka World Series in 2027 [4].

race_quality.explanation: Solid organization with a late-information habit. The wet-weather route is planned in advance, but routes and aid locations go public only in early August, weeks before the start [2].

experience.explanation: Enjoyable rather than unforgettable. The cyclocross-style finish and orchard party give it personality [6], while heat and a chaotic urban section can wear riders down late in the day [7].

community.explanation: A good local scene built around teams. The long routes can be raced solo or as a team of three [3], a format borrowed from sister event Rule of Three in Bentonville [6].

field_depth.explanation: Pros show up. The 2026 Pro/Elite race paid $15,000 [5], Geerike Schreurs won it solo and Tobias Kongstad won the sprint [8], and 2027 adds a Traka World Series round worth EUR 8,000 [4].

value.explanation: Fair, pending a price. 2027 fees are not out yet [1]; the entry buys four distances, a team category and a festival weekend [2][3].

expenses.explanation: Reasonable. A Midwestern college town with camping near the venue [5] keeps lodging cheap for anyone who can drive in; 2027 entry fees are not yet published [1].
